source.text: וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֔וּ צָרֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה וּבִנְיָמִ֑ן כִּֽי־בְנֵ֤י הַגּוֹלָה֙ בּוֹנִ֣ים הֵיכָ֔ל לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard [the] adversaries of Judah and Benjamin that [the] sons of the exile [were] building a temple for YHWH [the] God of Israel.

en.L: And the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the sons of the exile were building a temple for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel.
en.B: The enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the returned exiles were building a temple for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel.
en.R: The enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the people who came back from exile were building a temple for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

es.L: Y oyeron los adversarios de Judá y de Benjamín que los hijos del destierro edificaban un templo {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel.
es.B: Los enemigos de Judá y de Benjamín oyeron que los que habían vuelto del destierro estaban edificando un templo {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel.
es.R: Los enemigos de Judá y de Benjamín se enteraron de que los que regresaron del destierro estaban construyendo un templo {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel.

fr.L: Et les adversaires de Juda et de Benjamin apprirent que les fils de l’exil bâtissaient un temple {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël.
fr.B: Les ennemis de Juda et de Benjamin apprirent que les exilés revenus bâtissaient un temple {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël.
fr.R: Les ennemis de Juda et de Benjamin ont appris que les gens revenus de l’exil construisaient un temple {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël.

sw.L: Na adui za Yuda na Benyamini wakasikia kwamba wana wa uhamisho walikuwa wakimjengea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa Israeli hekalu.
sw.B: Adui za Yuda na Benyamini walisikia kwamba waliorudi kutoka uhamishoni walikuwa wakimjengea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa Israeli hekalu.
sw.R: Adui za Yuda na Benyamini walisikia kwamba watu waliorudi kutoka uhamishoni walikuwa wakimjengea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, hekalu.

vi.L: Và những kẻ thù của Giu-đa và Bên-gia-min nghe rằng con cái của những người lưu đày đang xây đền thờ cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: Những kẻ thù của Giu-đa và Bên-gia-min nghe tin những người lưu đày trở về đang xây đền thờ cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Những kẻ thù của Giu-đa và Bên-gia-min nghe tin những người từ chốn lưu đày trở về đang xây đền thờ cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên.

ko.L: 그리고 유다와 베냐민의 대적들이, 포로의 자손들이 이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 위하여 성전을 짓고 있다는 것을 들었다.
ko.B: 유다와 베냐민의 원수들은 포로에서 돌아온 사람들이 이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 위하여 성전을 짓고 있다는 소식을 들었다.
ko.R: 유다와 베냐민의 원수들은 포로로 끌려갔다가 돌아온 사람들이 이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 위해 성전을 짓고 있다는 소식을 들었다.

pt.L: E os adversários de Judá e Benjamim ouviram que os filhos do exílio estavam edificando um templo {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, o Deus de Israel.
pt.B: Os inimigos de Judá e Benjamim ouviram que os exilados que voltaram estavam construindo um templo {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, o Deus de Israel.
pt.R: Os inimigos de Judá e Benjamim ouviram que os que voltaram do exílio estavam construindo um templo {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, o Deus de Israel.

decisions.choice: the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin: those who opposed the returned community
decisions.reason: The writer calls them adversaries from the start, before they say a word. They are the people of verse 2, settled in the land by the kings of Assyria, and later the officials of Samaria (verses 9-10, 17). Judah and Benjamin are the two tribes whose land the exiles came back to (1:5).

decisions.choice: the sons of the exile: the community of those who returned from Babylon
decisions.reason: "Sons of" here means members of a group. In Ezra the phrase names the returned exiles as a community (6:19-20; 8:35; 10:7, 16).

decisions.choice: the returned exiles (Balanced); the people who came back from exile (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Ezra term list gives these wordings; Literal keeps "the sons of the exile".

decisions.choice: "los hijos del destierro" (L); "los que habían vuelto del destierro" (B); "los que regresaron del destierro" (R)
decisions.reason: The terms note's wording for *bene haggolah*, the community of the return, used through Ezra.

decisions.choice: "wana wa uhamisho" (L); "waliorudi kutoka uhamishoni" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The terms note's wording for the returned community, used through the book.

decisions.choice: con cái của những người lưu đày (Literal); những người lưu đày trở về (Balanced); những người từ chốn lưu đày trở về (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book's name for the returned community (m2), worded at each level as the terms note gives it and kept through Ezra.

decisions.choice: "포로의 자손들" (L), "포로에서 돌아온 사람들" (B), "포로로 끌려갔다가 돌아온 사람들" (R) for *bene haggolah*
decisions.reason: The terms note's forms for the returned exiles through Ezra; "자손들" at Literal means the members of the community, not literal sons, as the meaning decision says.

decisions.choice: os filhos do exílio (L); os exilados que voltaram (B); os que voltaram do exílio (R)
decisions.reason: For Ezra-Nehemiah: the community of the return (m2) has one wording per level, following the English levels; "repatriados" is a modern administrative word.

source.text: וַיִּגְּשׁ֨וּ אֶל־זְרֻבָּבֶ֜ל וְאֶל־רָאשֵׁ֣י הָֽאָב֗וֹת וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ לָהֶם֙ נִבְנֶ֣ה עִמָּכֶ֔ם כִּ֣י כָכֶ֔ם נִדְר֖וֹשׁ לֵֽאלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם וְל֣וֹ׀אֲנַ֣חְנוּ זֹבְחִ֗ים מִימֵי֙ אֵסַ֤ר חַדֹּן֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר הַמַּעֲלֶ֥ה אֹתָ֖נוּ פֹּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they approached Zerubbabel and [the] heads of the fathers and said to them, let us build with you, for like you we seek your God, and to him we [have been] sacrificing since [the] days of Esarhaddon king of Assyria, who brought us up here.

en.L: And they approached Zerubbabel and the heads of the fathers' [houses] and said to them, "Let us build with you, for like you we seek your God, and we have been sacrificing to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} since the days of Esarhaddon king of Assyria, who brought us up here."
en.B: So they came to Zerubbabel and the heads of families and said to them, "Let us build with you, for we worship your God as you do, and we have been sacrificing to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} ever since the days of Esarhaddon king of Assyria, who brought us here."
en.R: So they came to Zerubbabel and the family leaders and said, "Let us help you build, because we worship your God just as you do. We have been offering sacrifices to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} ever since King Esarhaddon of Assyria brought us here."

es.L: Y se acercaron a Zorobabel y a los jefes de las [casas] paternas y les dijeron: «Edifiquemos con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, porque como {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} buscamos a {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}, y a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hemos ofrecido sacrificios desde los días de Esarhadón rey de Asiria, que nos hizo subir aquí».
es.B: Entonces se acercaron a Zorobabel y a los jefes de familia y les dijeron: «{{plural_you:Déjennos|Dejadnos}} edificar con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, porque adoramos a {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}} como {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} hemos ofrecido sacrificios desde los días de Esarhadón rey de Asiria, que nos trajo aquí».
es.R: Entonces fueron a ver a Zorobabel y a los jefes de familia y les dijeron: «{{plural_you:Déjennos|Dejadnos}} ayudar{{plural_you:les|os}} a construir, porque adoramos a {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}} igual que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Desde que el rey Esarhadón de Asiria nos trajo aquí, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} hemos ofrecido sacrificios».

fr.L: Et ils s’approchèrent de Zorobabel et des chefs des pères et leur dirent : « Laissez-nous bâtir avec vous, car, comme vous, nous recherchons votre Dieu, et c’est à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} que nous sacrifions depuis les jours d’Assarhaddon, roi d’Assyrie, qui nous a fait monter ici. »
fr.B: Ils vinrent donc trouver Zorobabel et les chefs des familles et leur dirent : « Laissez-nous bâtir avec vous, car nous adorons votre Dieu comme vous, et nous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} offrons des sacrifices depuis le temps d’Assarhaddon, roi d’Assyrie, qui nous a amenés ici. »
fr.R: Ils sont donc venus trouver Zorobabel et les chefs de famille et leur ont dit : « Laissez-nous vous aider à construire, car nous adorons votre Dieu comme vous. Nous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} offrons des sacrifices depuis que le roi Assarhaddon d’Assyrie nous a amenés ici. »

sw.L: Wakamkaribia Zerubabeli na wakuu wa [nyumba za] baba, wakawaambia, "Tujenge pamoja nanyi, kwa maana kama ninyi tunamtafuta Mungu wenu, na tumekuwa tukimtolea {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} dhabihu tangu siku za Esar-hadoni mfalme wa Ashuru, aliyetupandisha hapa."
sw.B: Basi wakamjia Zerubabeli na wakuu wa jamaa, wakawaambia, "Tujenge pamoja nanyi, kwa maana tunamwabudu Mungu wenu kama ninyi, na tumekuwa tukimtolea {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} dhabihu tangu siku za Esar-hadoni mfalme wa Ashuru, aliyetuleta hapa."
sw.R: Basi wakamjia Zerubabeli na viongozi wa jamaa, wakasema, "Tuwasaidie kujenga, kwa sababu tunamwabudu Mungu wenu kama ninyi. Tumekuwa tukimtolea {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} dhabihu tangu Mfalme Esar-hadoni wa Ashuru alipotuleta hapa."

vi.L: Và họ đến gần Xô-rô-ba-bên và những người đứng đầu các gia tộc và nói với họ: "Hãy để chúng tôi xây cùng các ông, vì như các ông, chúng tôi tìm kiếm Đức Chúa Trời của các ông, và chúng tôi vẫn dâng tế lễ cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} từ những ngày của Ê-sạt-ha-đôn vua A-si-ri, là người đã đem chúng tôi lên đây."
vi.B: Vậy họ đến gặp Xô-rô-ba-bên và các trưởng tộc mà nói: "Hãy cho chúng tôi cùng xây với các ông, vì chúng tôi cũng thờ phượng Đức Chúa Trời của các ông như các ông, và chúng tôi vẫn dâng tế lễ cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} từ thời Ê-sạt-ha-đôn vua A-si-ri, là người đã đưa chúng tôi đến đây."
vi.R: Vậy họ đến gặp Xô-rô-ba-bên và những người đứng đầu các gia đình mà nói: "Hãy để chúng tôi giúp các ông xây, vì chúng tôi cũng thờ phượng Đức Chúa Trời của các ông như các ông. Chúng tôi vẫn dâng tế lễ cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} từ khi vua Ê-sạt-ha-đôn của A-si-ri đưa chúng tôi đến đây."

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 스룹바벨과 조상들의 [집의] 우두머리들에게 다가와서 그들에게 말했다. "우리도 당신들과 함께 짓게 해 주십시오. 우리도 당신들처럼 당신들의 하나님을 찾고 있으며, 우리를 이곳으로 올라오게 한 앗시리아 왕 에살핫돈의 때부터 그분께 제사를 드려 왔습니다."
ko.B: 그래서 그들은 스룹바벨과 집안 우두머리들에게 와서 말했다. "우리도 여러분과 함께 짓게 해 주십시오. 우리도 여러분처럼 여러분의 하나님을 섬기고 있고, 앗시리아 왕 에살핫돈이 우리를 이곳으로 데려온 때부터 그분께 제사를 드려 왔습니다."
ko.R: 그래서 그들은 스룹바벨과 집안 지도자들에게 와서 말했다. "우리도 성전 짓는 일을 돕게 해 주십시오. 우리도 여러분처럼 여러분의 하나님을 섬깁니다. 앗시리아 왕 에살핫돈이 우리를 이곳으로 데려온 뒤로 우리는 계속 그분께 제사를 드려 왔습니다."

pt.L: E se aproximaram de Zorobabel e dos chefes dos pais e lhes disseram: "Edifiquemos com vocês, porque, como vocês, buscamos o Deus de vocês, e a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} temos oferecido sacrifícios desde os dias de Esar-Hadom, rei da Assíria, que nos fez subir para cá."
pt.B: Por isso vieram a Zorobabel e aos chefes das famílias e lhes disseram: "Vamos construir com vocês, pois adoramos o Deus de vocês, como vocês, e temos oferecido sacrifícios a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} desde os dias de Esar-Hadom, rei da Assíria, que nos trouxe para cá."
pt.R: Por isso eles foram até Zorobabel e os chefes das famílias e disseram: "Deixem que nós ajudemos vocês a construir, porque adoramos o Deus de vocês, assim como vocês. Temos oferecido sacrifícios a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} desde que o rei Esar-Hadom, da Assíria, nos trouxe para cá."

decisions.choice: Esarhaddon king of Assyria: the king who settled them here
decisions.reason: Esarhaddon ruled Assyria from 681 to 669 BC. After the northern kingdom fell in 722 BC the kings of Assyria moved peoples from other lands into the cities of Samaria. They learned to worship the LORD but went on serving their own gods as well (2 Kings 17:24-41).

decisions.choice: to him we sacrifice: the reading of the Hebrew margin
alternatives: and we have not sacrificed since the days of Esarhaddon
decisions.reason: The written text has a word meaning "not", which would give "and we have not been sacrificing" since Esarhaddon's days. The scribes' marginal reading, followed here, has a word that sounds the same and means "to him". The marginal reading fits the claim the speakers are making.

decisions.choice: we seek your God: we worship him
decisions.reason: To "seek" God is to turn to him in worship and prayer (Deuteronomy 4:29; Psalm 105:4). They claim to share the returned exiles' faith; 2 Kings 17:33 says such settlers feared the LORD and served their own gods too.

decisions.choice: the heads of the fathers: heads of families
decisions.reason: As in 3:12, "the fathers" stands for the fathers' houses, the extended families.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to God, so it takes the deity pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun on "él" (L) and "le" (B, R); plural_you for "you"
decisions.reason: The English spans the pronoun for God, and Spanish spans its free pronoun at every level; the speakers address the leaders together, so "you" is the plural setting. Esarhaddon as in 2 Kings 19:37 ("Esarhadón").

decisions.choice: the free pronoun "yeye" added after "tukimtolea" to carry the deity span
decisions.reason: The object is marked inside the verb ("-m-"), which cannot take a capital; Swahili may add the free pronoun for emphasis, and it carries the span the English has.

decisions.choice: chúng tôi / các ông
decisions.reason: The settlers speak to the leaders of Judah as equals they hope to join: "chúng tôi" for themselves (excluding the hearers) and "các ông" for them. The leaders answer in the same terms in verse 3.

decisions.choice: The settlers speak in polite 합쇼체 with "당신들" (L) or "여러분" (B, R)
decisions.reason: They come asking a favor of the community's leaders, so Korean has them speak politely; the honorific "그분" for God carries the English deity pronoun, which has no Korean span.

decisions.choice: "에살핫돈", "앗시리아"
decisions.reason: The usual Protestant spelling of the name; 앗시리아 as in the Kings–Chronicles name table.

decisions.choice: o Deus de vocês; Esar-Hadom
decisions.reason: "O Deus de vocês" where "o seu Deus" could be read as "their God" (style section 11); "Esar-Hadom" as 2 Kings 19:37 in Portuguese (m1).

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ לָהֶ֨ם זְרֻבָּבֶ֜ל וְיֵשׁ֗וּעַ וּשְׁאָ֨ר רָאשֵׁ֤י הָֽאָבוֹת֙ לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לֹֽא־לָ֣כֶם וָלָ֔נוּ לִבְנ֥וֹת בַּ֖יִת לֵאלֹהֵ֑ינוּ כִּי֩ אֲנַ֨חְנוּ יַ֜חַד נִבְנֶ֗ה לַֽיהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֔נוּ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ כּ֥וֹרֶשׁ מֶֽלֶךְ־פָּרָֽס׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to them Zerubbabel and Jeshua and [the] rest of [the] heads of the fathers of Israel, not for you and for us to build a house for our God, for we together will build for YHWH [the] God of Israel, as commanded us the king Cyrus, king of Persia.

en.L: And Zerubbabel and Jeshua and the rest of the heads of the fathers' [houses] of Israel said to them, "[It is] not for you and for us to build a house for our God, but we ourselves together will build for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel, as King Cyrus the king of Persia commanded us."
en.B: But Zerubbabel, Jeshua and the rest of the heads of the families of Israel said to them, "You have no part with us in building a house for our God. We alone will build it for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel, as King Cyrus, the king of Persia, commanded us."
en.R: But Zerubbabel, Jeshua and the other leaders of the families of Israel answered, "You have no part in building a temple for our God. We will build it ourselves for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, as King Cyrus of Persia commanded us."

es.L: Y Zorobabel y Jesúa y los demás jefes de las [casas] paternas de Israel les dijeron: «No [es] para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y para nosotros edificar una casa a nuestro Dios, sino que nosotros juntos edificaremos {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel, como nos mandó el rey Ciro, rey de Persia».
es.B: Pero Zorobabel, Jesúa y los demás jefes de las familias de Israel les dijeron: «{{plural_you:Ustedes no tienen|Vosotros no tenéis}} parte con nosotros en edificar una casa a nuestro Dios. Nosotros solos la edificaremos {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel, como nos mandó el rey Ciro, rey de Persia».
es.R: Pero Zorobabel, Jesúa y los otros jefes de las familias de Israel les respondieron: «{{plural_you:Ustedes no tienen|Vosotros no tenéis}} nada que ver en la construcción de un templo para nuestro Dios. Nosotros mismos lo construiremos para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel, como nos lo mandó el rey Ciro de Persia».

fr.L: Et Zorobabel et Yeshoua et le reste des chefs des pères d’Israël leur dirent : « [Ce n’est] pas à vous et à nous de bâtir une maison pour notre Dieu, mais nous, nous bâtirons ensemble pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël, comme nous l’a ordonné le roi Cyrus, roi de Perse. »
fr.B: Mais Zorobabel, Yeshoua et les autres chefs des familles d’Israël leur répondirent : « Vous n’avez aucune part avec nous dans la construction d’une maison pour notre Dieu. Nous seuls la bâtirons pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël, comme nous l’a ordonné le roi Cyrus, roi de Perse. »
fr.R: Mais Zorobabel, Yeshoua et les autres chefs des familles d’Israël leur ont répondu : « Vous n’avez rien à voir dans la construction d’un temple pour notre Dieu. Nous le construirons nous-mêmes pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël, comme le roi Cyrus de Perse nous l’a ordonné. »

sw.L: Lakini Zerubabeli na Yeshua na wakuu wengine wa [nyumba za] baba wa Israeli wakawaambia, "Si [kazi] yenu na yetu kumjengea Mungu wetu nyumba, bali sisi wenyewe pamoja tutamjengea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa Israeli, kama mfalme Koreshi mfalme wa Uajemi alivyotuamuru."
sw.B: Lakini Zerubabeli, Yeshua na wakuu wengine wa jamaa za Israeli wakawaambia, "Ninyi hamna sehemu pamoja nasi katika kumjengea Mungu wetu nyumba. Sisi peke yetu tutamjengea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa Israeli, kama Mfalme Koreshi, mfalme wa Uajemi, alivyotuamuru."
sw.R: Lakini Zerubabeli, Yeshua na viongozi wengine wa jamaa za Israeli wakajibu, "Ninyi hamna sehemu katika kumjengea Mungu wetu hekalu. Sisi wenyewe tutamjengea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, kama Mfalme Koreshi wa Uajemi alivyotuamuru."

vi.L: Và Xô-rô-ba-bên, Giê-sua và những người đứng đầu các gia tộc còn lại của Y-sơ-ra-ên nói với họ: "[Không phải việc] của các ông và của chúng tôi để xây một ngôi nhà cho Đức Chúa Trời chúng tôi, nhưng chính chúng tôi cùng nhau sẽ xây cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, như vua Si-ru, vua Ba Tư, đã truyền cho chúng tôi."
vi.B: Nhưng Xô-rô-ba-bên, Giê-sua và các trưởng tộc khác của Y-sơ-ra-ên đáp: "Các ông không có phần gì với chúng tôi trong việc xây nhà cho Đức Chúa Trời chúng tôi. Một mình chúng tôi sẽ xây cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, như vua Si-ru, vua Ba Tư, đã truyền cho chúng tôi."
vi.R: Nhưng Xô-rô-ba-bên, Giê-sua và những người đứng đầu các gia đình khác của Y-sơ-ra-ên trả lời: "Các ông không có phần gì trong việc xây đền thờ cho Đức Chúa Trời chúng tôi. Chính chúng tôi sẽ xây cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, như vua Si-ru của Ba Tư đã truyền cho chúng tôi."

ko.L: 그러나 스룹바벨과 예수아와 이스라엘의 조상들의 [집의] 나머지 우두머리들이 그들에게 말했다. "우리 하나님의 집을 짓는 것은 당신들과 우리가 [함께 할 일이] 아닙니다. 페르시아 왕 고레스 왕이 우리에게 명령한 대로, 우리가 함께 이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 위하여 지을 것입니다."
ko.B: 그러나 스룹바벨과 예수아와 이스라엘의 나머지 집안 우두머리들이 그들에게 말했다. "우리 하나님의 집을 짓는 일에 여러분은 우리와 함께할 몫이 없습니다. 페르시아 왕 고레스께서 우리에게 명령하신 대로, 우리끼리 이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 위해 지을 것입니다."
ko.R: 그러나 스룹바벨과 예수아와 이스라엘의 다른 집안 지도자들은 이렇게 대답했다. "여러분은 우리 하나님의 성전을 짓는 일에 끼어들 수 없습니다. 페르시아 왕 고레스께서 우리에게 명령하신 대로, 이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전은 우리가 직접 지을 것입니다."

pt.L: E Zorobabel e Jesua e o restante dos chefes dos pais de Israel lhes disseram: "Não [cabe] a vocês e a nós edificar uma casa para o nosso Deus, mas nós mesmos, juntos, edificaremos {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, o Deus de Israel, como nos ordenou o rei Ciro, rei da Pérsia."
pt.B: Mas Zorobabel, Jesua e os demais chefes das famílias de Israel lhes responderam: "Vocês não têm parte conosco na construção de uma casa para o nosso Deus. Somente nós a construiremos {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, o Deus de Israel, como nos ordenou o rei Ciro, rei da Pérsia."
pt.R: Mas Zorobabel, Jesua e os outros chefes das famílias de Israel responderam: "Vocês não têm parte na construção de um templo para o nosso Deus. Nós mesmos vamos construí-lo {{divine_name:para o SENHOR|para Javé}}, o Deus de Israel, como o rei Ciro, da Pérsia, nos ordenou."

decisions.choice: not for you and for us: you have no share with us
decisions.reason: "Not for you and for us" is a way of saying the two groups have nothing in common in this work (compare 2 Kings 9:18, "what is it to you", and Nehemiah 2:20, "you have no share").

decisions.choice: we together will build: we by ourselves
decisions.reason: The word means "together" or "as one"; set against "you" it means the returned exiles alone, as one body.

decisions.choice: as Cyrus commanded us: the decree was for his people
decisions.reason: Cyrus's decree invited those "among you of all his people" to go up and build (1:3), and it was the returned exiles who went. The leaders answer by appealing to the king's own terms. Verse 1 has already called those who asked adversaries, and verses 4-5 show what they did next.

decisions.choice: You have no part with us in (Balanced); You have no part in (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the short Hebrew phrase; Literal keeps its form with a bracketed verb.

decisions.choice: "고레스께서 ... 명령하신" (B, R): the leaders speak of the king with the honorific
decisions.reason: Speaking of their sovereign before others, the leaders would show him respect; Literal keeps the plain form of the narrative.

source.text: וַיְהִי֙ עַם־הָאָ֔רֶץ מְרַפִּ֖ים יְדֵ֣י עַם־יְהוּדָ֑ה וּֽמְבַהֲלִ֥ים אוֹתָ֖ם לִבְנֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was [that the] people of the land [were] weakening [the] hands of [the] people of Judah and terrifying them from building,

en.L: And it was that the people of the land were weakening the hands of the people of Judah and making them afraid to build,
en.B: Then the people of the land set about discouraging the people of Judah and making them afraid to build,
en.R: So the people living in the land tried to discourage the people of Judah and frighten them so they would stop building.

es.L: Y sucedió que el pueblo de la tierra debilitaba las manos del pueblo de Judá y lo atemorizaba para que no edificara,
es.B: Entonces el pueblo de la tierra se dedicó a desanimar al pueblo de Judá y a atemorizarlo para que no edificara,
es.R: Así que la gente que vivía en el país trató de desanimar al pueblo de Judá y de asustarlo para que dejara de construir.

fr.L: Et il arriva que le peuple du pays affaiblissait les mains du peuple de Juda et l’effrayait pour qu’il ne bâtisse pas,
fr.B: Alors le peuple du pays se mit à décourager le peuple de Juda et à l’effrayer pour qu’il ne bâtisse pas,
fr.R: Alors les gens qui habitaient dans le pays ont essayé de décourager le peuple de Juda et de lui faire peur pour qu’il arrête de construire.

sw.L: Na ikawa kwamba watu wa nchi walikuwa wakiidhoofisha mikono ya watu wa Yuda na kuwatia hofu wasijenge,
sw.B: Ndipo watu wa nchi wakaanza kuwavunja moyo watu wa Yuda na kuwatia hofu wasijenge,
sw.R: Kwa hiyo watu walioishi katika nchi walijaribu kuwavunja moyo watu wa Yuda na kuwatisha ili waache kujenga.

vi.L: Và dân của xứ làm yếu tay dân Giu-đa và làm cho họ sợ hãi không dám xây,
vi.B: Bấy giờ dân của xứ tìm cách làm cho dân Giu-đa nản lòng và sợ hãi không dám xây,
vi.R: Vì vậy, những dân đang sống trong xứ tìm cách làm cho dân Giu-đa nản lòng và sợ hãi để họ thôi không xây nữa.

ko.L: 그리고 그 땅의 백성이 유다 백성의 손을 약하게 하고, 그들이 짓지 못하도록 겁을 주었다.
ko.B: 그러자 그 땅의 백성은 유다 백성의 기를 꺾고, 그들이 짓지 못하도록 겁을 주었다.
ko.R: 그 땅에 사는 사람들은 유다 백성의 힘을 빼고 겁을 주어 성전 짓는 일을 그만두게 하려고 했다.

pt.L: E aconteceu que o povo da terra enfraquecia as mãos do povo de Judá e o aterrorizava para que não edificasse,
pt.B: Então o povo da terra se pôs a desanimar o povo de Judá e a amedrontá-lo para que não construísse,
pt.R: Por isso o povo que vivia na terra tentou desanimar o povo de Judá e assustá-lo para que parasse de construir.

decisions.choice: the people of the land: the populations outside the returned community
decisions.reason: As in 3:3, the phrase means those who were not among the returned exiles, here the same people who asked to build in verse 2. Elsewhere it can mean the ordinary landholders of Judah (2 Kings 11:14), but in Ezra and Nehemiah it marks those outside the community of the return (9:1; 10:2).

decisions.choice: weakening the hands: discouraging them
decisions.reason: Hands that hang down picture people who have lost heart (Jeremiah 38:4; Nehemiah 6:9). The participles describe something they kept doing.

decisions.choice: terrifying them from building: making them afraid to build
decisions.reason: The Hebrew margin and the written text differ slightly in the form of this verb, but both mean to frighten or alarm.

decisions.choice: the people living in the land
decisions.reason: Readable follows the Ezra term list, as in 3:3.

decisions.choice: ending with a comma
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into verse 5, so Literal and Balanced end the record with a comma; Readable ends its own sentence here.

decisions.choice: "el pueblo de la tierra" (L, B); "la gente que vivía en el país" (R); "debilitaba las manos" (L); "desanimar" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As at 3:3, the terms note's wording for the people of the land; Literal keeps the idiom of weak hands, and the other levels give its sense (m2).

decisions.choice: "kuwavunja moyo" (B, R); Literal keeps "kuidhoofisha mikono"
decisions.reason: Weakening someone's hands means taking away their will to work; "kuvunja moyo" is the Swahili for discouraging.

decisions.choice: làm yếu tay
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of weakening their hands; Balanced and Readable say what it means, "làm cho ... nản lòng" (m2).

decisions.choice: "그 땅의 백성" (L, B), "그 땅에 사는 사람들" (R)
decisions.reason: The terms note's forms for *ʿam haʾarets*, as at 3:3.

decisions.choice: The Korean sentence ends here
alternatives: A comma running on into verse 5
decisions.reason: Korean puts the verb last, so the English run-on into verse 5 cannot be copied; verse 5 starts its own sentence with "또".

decisions.choice: o povo da terra (L, B); o povo que vivia na terra (R)
decisions.reason: As 3:3: the singular "povo da terra" where the Hebrew has the singular (m1), Readable as the English Readable.

source.text: וְסֹכְרִ֧ים עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם יוֹעֲצִ֖ים לְהָפֵ֣ר עֲצָתָ֑ם כָּל־יְמֵ֗י כּ֚וֹרֶשׁ מֶ֣לֶךְ פָּרַ֔ס וְעַד־מַלְכ֖וּת דָּרְיָ֥וֶשׁ מֶֽלֶךְ־פָּרָֽס׃

records.literal_gloss: and hiring against them counselors to frustrate their purpose all [the] days of Cyrus king of Persia and until [the] reign of Darius king of Persia.

en.L: and hiring counselors against them to frustrate their purpose all the days of Cyrus king of Persia and until the reign of Darius king of Persia.
en.B: and they bribed officials against them to frustrate their plans throughout the reign of Cyrus king of Persia and until the reign of Darius king of Persia.
en.R: They paid officials to work against them and spoil their plans. This went on as long as Cyrus was king of Persia and until Darius became king.

es.L: y sobornaba consejeros contra ellos para frustrar su propósito todos los días de Ciro rey de Persia y hasta el reinado de Darío rey de Persia.
es.B: y sobornaron a funcionarios contra ellos para frustrar sus planes durante todo el reinado de Ciro rey de Persia y hasta el reinado de Darío rey de Persia.
es.R: Pagaron a funcionarios para que trabajaran contra ellos y echaran a perder sus planes. Esto continuó mientras Ciro fue rey de Persia y hasta que Darío llegó a ser rey.

fr.L: et ils payaient contre eux des conseillers pour faire échouer leur projet, pendant tous les jours de Cyrus, roi de Perse, et jusqu’au règne de Darius, roi de Perse.
fr.B: et ils soudoyèrent des fonctionnaires contre eux pour faire échouer leurs projets pendant tout le règne de Cyrus, roi de Perse, et jusqu’au règne de Darius, roi de Perse.
fr.R: Ils ont payé des fonctionnaires pour agir contre eux et faire échouer leurs projets. Cela a duré pendant tout le règne de Cyrus, roi de Perse, et jusqu’à ce que Darius devienne roi.

sw.L: na kuajiri washauri dhidi yao ili kulivunja kusudi lao siku zote za Koreshi mfalme wa Uajemi na mpaka utawala wa Dario mfalme wa Uajemi.
sw.B: nao wakawahonga maafisa dhidi yao ili kuyavuruga mipango yao wakati wote wa utawala wa Koreshi mfalme wa Uajemi mpaka utawala wa Dario mfalme wa Uajemi.
sw.R: Waliwalipa maafisa wafanye kazi dhidi yao na kuiharibu mipango yao. Jambo hili liliendelea wakati wote Koreshi alipokuwa mfalme wa Uajemi, mpaka Dario alipokuwa mfalme.

vi.L: và thuê những người cố vấn chống lại họ để phá hỏng ý định của họ suốt mọi ngày của Si-ru vua Ba Tư và cho đến triều đại Đa-ri-út vua Ba Tư.
vi.B: và họ hối lộ các quan chức để chống lại dân Giu-đa, phá hỏng kế hoạch của họ suốt thời Si-ru vua Ba Tư cho đến triều đại Đa-ri-út vua Ba Tư.
vi.R: Họ trả tiền cho các quan chức để chống lại dân Giu-đa và phá hỏng kế hoạch của họ. Việc ấy kéo dài suốt thời Si-ru làm vua Ba Tư, cho đến khi Đa-ri-út lên làm vua.

ko.L: 또 페르시아 왕 고레스의 모든 날 동안 페르시아 왕 다리오의 통치 때까지, 그들은 그들을 대적하는 조언자들을 고용하여 그들의 계획을 좌절시켰다.
ko.B: 또 그들은 페르시아 왕 고레스가 다스리는 동안 내내, 그리고 페르시아 왕 다리오가 다스릴 때까지, 관리들을 매수하여 유다 백성의 계획을 방해했다.
ko.R: 그들은 관리들에게 돈을 주어 유다 백성의 계획을 망치게 했다. 이런 일은 고레스가 페르시아 왕으로 있는 동안 내내 이어졌고, 다리오가 왕이 될 때까지 계속되었다.

pt.L: e contratava conselheiros contra eles para frustrar o seu plano, todos os dias de Ciro, rei da Pérsia, até o reinado de Dario, rei da Pérsia.
pt.B: e subornaram oficiais contra eles para frustrar os seus planos durante todo o reinado de Ciro, rei da Pérsia, até o reinado de Dario, rei da Pérsia.
pt.R: Eles pagaram oficiais para trabalhar contra o povo de Judá e estragar os seus planos. Isso continuou durante todo o tempo em que Ciro foi rei da Pérsia e até Dario se tornar rei.

decisions.choice: hiring counselors: paying advisers or officials to act against them
decisions.reason: The counselors are most likely people with influence at the Persian court or in the provincial government, paid to block the work. "Hire" is used of bribing a prophet in Nehemiah 6:12-13.

decisions.choice: from Cyrus to Darius: about eighteen years
decisions.reason: Cyrus ruled the Persian empire from 539 to 530 BC and Darius I from 522 to 486 BC. Work on the temple stopped until the second year of Darius, 520 BC (verse 24; Haggai 1:1-2).

decisions.choice: until the reign of Darius: the account moves ahead
decisions.reason: This verse sums up the whole time of opposition to the temple. Verses 6-23 then go further ahead to later kings, Ahasuerus and Artaxerxes, and to opposition against the city walls; verse 24 comes back to the temple under Darius.

decisions.choice: bribed officials
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "hiring counselors against them" amounted to; Literal keeps the words. Readable says "paid officials".

decisions.choice: "sobornaba consejeros" (L); "sobornaron a funcionarios" (B); "pagaron a funcionarios" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is to hire; with people paid to work against others Spanish "sobornar" carries the sense the English gives at Balanced (m1), and Literal keeps "consejeros".

decisions.choice: "wakawahonga maafisa" (B); "kuajiri washauri" (L); "waliwalipa maafisa" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English: Balanced says what hiring counsellors against them amounted to.

decisions.choice: "payaient" (imperfect)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew participles describe something done again and again over years, so Literal uses the French imperfect, as the narrative rule for repeated action does.

source.text: וּבְמַלְכוּת֙ אֲחַשְׁוֵר֔וֹשׁ בִּתְחִלַּ֖ת מַלְכוּת֑וֹ כָּתְב֣וּ שִׂטְנָ֔ה עַל־יֹשְׁבֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And in [the] reign of Ahasuerus, in [the] beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against [the] inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.

en.L: And in the reign of Ahasuerus, in the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.
en.B: In the reign of Ahasuerus, at the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the people living in Judah and Jerusalem.
en.R: Later, when Ahasuerus became king, they wrote a letter accusing the people of Judah and Jerusalem.

es.L: Y en el reinado de Asuero, al principio de su reinado, escribieron una acusación contra los habitantes de Judá y de Jerusalén.
es.B: En el reinado de Asuero, al comienzo de su reinado, escribieron una acusación contra los que vivían en Judá y en Jerusalén.
es.R: Más tarde, cuando Asuero llegó a ser rey, escribieron una carta en la que acusaban al pueblo de Judá y de Jerusalén.

fr.L: Et sous le règne d’Assuérus, au commencement de son règne, ils écrivirent une accusation contre les habitants de Juda et de Jérusalem.
fr.B: Sous le règne d’Assuérus, au début de son règne, ils écrivirent une accusation contre les habitants de Juda et de Jérusalem.
fr.R: Plus tard, quand Assuérus est devenu roi, ils ont écrit une lettre pour accuser les gens de Juda et de Jérusalem.

sw.L: Na katika utawala wa Ahasuero, mwanzoni mwa utawala wake, wakaandika mashtaka dhidi ya wakazi wa Yuda na Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Katika utawala wa Ahasuero, mwanzoni mwa utawala wake, waliandika mashtaka dhidi ya watu walioishi Yuda na Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Baadaye, Ahasuero alipokuwa mfalme, waliandika barua ya kuwashtaki watu wa Yuda na Yerusalemu.

vi.L: Và trong triều đại A-suê-ru, vào lúc đầu triều đại của vua, họ viết một bản cáo trạng chống lại dân cư Giu-đa và Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.B: Dưới triều vua A-suê-ru, vào đầu triều đại của vua, họ viết một bản cáo trạng chống lại những người sống ở Giu-đa và Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.R: Về sau, khi A-suê-ru lên làm vua, họ viết thư tố cáo dân Giu-đa và Giê-ru-sa-lem.

ko.L: 그리고 아하수에로의 통치 때에, 그의 통치 초기에, 그들이 유다와 예루살렘 주민들을 고발하는 글을 썼다.
ko.B: 아하수에로가 다스리던 때, 그가 다스리기 시작할 무렵에, 그들은 유다와 예루살렘에 사는 사람들을 고발하는 글을 써 올렸다.
ko.R: 그 뒤 아하수에로가 왕이 되었을 때, 그들은 유다와 예루살렘 사람들을 고발하는 편지를 썼다.

pt.L: E no reinado de Assuero, no princípio do seu reinado, escreveram uma acusação contra os habitantes de Judá e Jerusalém.
pt.B: No reinado de Assuero, no começo do seu reinado, escreveram uma acusação contra os moradores de Judá e de Jerusalém.
pt.R: Mais tarde, quando Assuero se tornou rei, eles escreveram uma carta acusando o povo de Judá e de Jerusalém.

decisions.choice: Ahasuerus: the Persian king known in Greek as Xerxes

decisions.choice: Artaxerxes: Artaxerxes I, king of Persia
decisions.reason: This is most likely Artaxerxes I, who ruled from 465 to 424 BC, after Ahasuerus. Ezra (7:1) and Nehemiah (Nehemiah 2:1) came to Jerusalem in his reign. So verses 7-23 concern events some seventy or more years after the temple's foundation, and they are about the city and its walls (verses 12-13), not the temple.

decisions.choice: Bishlam: probably a personal name
decisions.reason: The word is taken here as the name of one of the writers, like Mithredath and Tabeel. It could also be read as "with the agreement of", that is, Mithredath wrote with Tabeel's approval.

decisions.choice: written in Aramaic script and translated into Aramaic
alternatives: was written in Aramaic and translated. [The following is in] Aramaic:
decisions.reason: The first "Aramaic" can be read as the script and the second as the language: the letter was written in Aramaic letters and set out in the Aramaic language, the official language of the Persian empire. Another reading takes the last word as a note to the reader, "Aramaic:", marking that the text from here (4:8-6:18) is itself in Aramaic; the verse would then end "written in Aramaic and translated".

decisions.choice: their associates
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "his associates", referring to the first named writer; Balanced and Readable say "their" ("with them") since three writers are named. Literal keeps "his".

decisions.choice: Aramaic [script] ... [into] Aramaic (Literal); Aramaic script ... into Aramaic (Balanced)
decisions.reason: English needs words to show the two senses of "Aramaic" that meaning decision m3 takes; Literal brackets them.

decisions.choice: "Artajerjes", "Bislam"; "en [caracteres] arameos y traducida [al] arameo" (L)
decisions.reason: Artaxerxes as the terms note gives it; Bishlam is taken as a name (m2). Spanish, like the English, needs words to show the two senses of "Aramaic" (m3); Literal brackets them.

decisions.choice: "kwa [herufi za] Kiaramu na kutafsiriwa [kwa] Kiaramu" (L); "herufi za Kiaramu ... kwa Kiaramu" (B); "herufi za Kiaramu na ... lugha ya Kiaramu" (R)
decisions.reason: Swahili, like English, needs words to show the script and the language that the meaning decision distinguishes; Literal brackets them.

decisions.choice: Ạt-ta-xét-xe; Bít-lam; Ta-bê-ên
decisions.reason: The Persian king is "Ạt-ta-xét-xe", as the terms note gives. Bishlam and Tabeel are spelled from the Hebrew; Mithredath is spelled as in 1:8, though he is probably another man.

decisions.choice: "아닥사스다", "비슬람", "미드르닷", "다브엘"
decisions.reason: The terms note's form for Artaxerxes; the other names follow the usual Protestant spellings (미드르닷 as at 1:8).

decisions.choice: "아람 [문자로] ... 아람 [말로]" (L); "아람 문자로 ... 아람 말로" (B)
decisions.reason: As the English, Korean needs a word to show the two senses the meaning decision takes, the script and the language; Literal brackets them.

decisions.reason: "Artaxerxes" (m1) and "Bislão", "Tabeel" in their usual Brazilian forms; "Mitredate" as 1:8. The two senses of "Aramaic" (m3) are given as script and language, with brackets at Literal, as the English does.

decisions.choice: the text changes from Hebrew to Aramaic
decisions.reason: From this verse to 6:18 the book is written in Aramaic, the language of the Persian empire's letters and records, which the Jews of the exile also spoke. The section quotes or follows official documents, beginning with this letter. The text returns to Hebrew at 6:19, and there is a second Aramaic section, the king's letter to Ezra, at 7:12-26.

decisions.choice: master of decree and the scribe: the senior official and the secretary
decisions.reason: "Master of decree" is a Persian title for a high official with authority to issue orders, perhaps the head of the provincial administration in Samaria. The scribe was the official secretary who wrote and kept the documents. Both seem to belong to the government of the province Beyond the River (verses 10, 17).

decisions.choice: a letter concerning Jerusalem: a letter against it
decisions.reason: The preposition means "about" or "against"; the letter (verses 11-16) is an accusation against the city. "One letter" is the Aramaic way of saying "a letter".

decisions.choice: the chief officer (Balanced, Readable); the commander (Literal)
decisions.reason: "Master of decree" is given an English official title; meaning decision m2 explains it. Readable calls Shimshai "the secretary" so the word is not confused with Ezra's title "scribe".

decisions.choice: "Rehúm el comandante" (L); "el oficial principal" (B, R); "Simsai el escriba" (L, B); "el secretario" (R)
decisions.reason: The terms note's names; the Persian title "master of decree" is "comandante" at Literal and an official title at Balanced and Readable, and Readable calls Shimshai "secretario" so that he is not confused with Ezra the scribe, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "mkuu wa amri" (L), "afisa mkuu" (B, R); "mwandishi" (L, B), "katibu" (R)
decisions.reason: The Persian titles as the terms note sets them; Readable's "katibu" keeps Shimshai apart from Ezra the "mwandishi" (scribe).

decisions.choice: "le commandant" (Literal), "le haut fonctionnaire" (Balanced, Readable); "le scribe" (Literal, Balanced), "le secrétaire" (Readable)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as the terms note: Rehum's Persian title and Shimshai's office, with "secrétaire" at Readable so that he is not taken for a scribe of the law like Ezra.

decisions.choice: quan chỉ huy (Literal); vị quan đứng đầu (Balanced, Readable); thư ký
alternatives: viên quan trưởng; thầy thông giáo
decisions.reason: "Master of decree" is a Persian title for a senior official (m2): "quan chỉ huy" at Literal, "vị quan đứng đầu" at Balanced and Readable. "Viên quan trưởng" is avoided because it is Rabshakeh's title in Kings. Shimshai is a royal secretary, "thư ký" as for Shebna in 2 Kings 18:18; Ezra the scribe is "thầy thông giáo".

decisions.choice: "사령관 르훔" (L), "고위 관리 르훔" (B, R); "서기관 심새" at every level
decisions.reason: The terms note's titles for the Persian officials; "서기관" stays at Readable too, where the English has "secretary", since Korean "서기관" is already the plain word for an official scribe.

decisions.choice: the same Portuguese for the Aramaic of 4:8-6:18
decisions.reason: The text changes to Aramaic here (m1) and returns to Hebrew at 6:19. The Portuguese does not mark the change in its wording: the Aramaic section is translated in the same words and register as the Hebrew around it ("a casa de Deus", "os anciãos dos judeus", "Além do Rio"), and the meaning decisions tell the reader where the language changes.

decisions.choice: o comandante (L), o oficial-chefe (B, R); o escriba (L, B), o secretário (R); Reum, Sinsai
decisions.reason: The Persian title (m2) is given an official's title, as the English does; Readable says "o secretário" so that it is not taken for Ezra's title "escriba".

decisions.choice: Then Rehum ...: the heading of the letter, naming its senders
decisions.reason: Verses 9-10 have no verb of their own. They list who sent the letter, in the manner of an official letter's heading, and carry on from "wrote" in verse 8. The list ends with "and now" at the end of verse 10.

decisions.choice: Dinaites, Apharsathchites, Tarpelites, Apharsites: uncertain names
alternatives: the judges, the envoys, the officials, the Persians
decisions.reason: These words are not known outside this book, and their meaning is uncertain. They may be peoples, like the names after them; but several may be Persian titles of officials: the first may mean judges, the second (compare 5:6; 6:6) a kind of envoy or official, and the fourth may mean Persians or a further rank of officials. They are kept as names here.

decisions.choice: Erech, Babylon, Susa and Elam: peoples brought from the east
decisions.reason: Erech (Uruk) and Babylon were old cities of Babylonia (Genesis 10:10). Susa was the capital of Elam, east of Babylonia, and later a royal city of Persia (Nehemiah 1:1; Esther 1:2). Peoples from these places had been settled in Samaria by the Assyrian kings (verse 10).

decisions.choice: the Dehavites: the reading of the Hebrew margin
alternatives: the people of Susa, that is, the Elamites
decisions.reason: The scribes' marginal reading gives a people's name, the Dehavites, otherwise unknown. The consonants of the written text can also be read as "that is", giving "the Susanchites, that is, the Elamites", which fits Susa being in Elam.

decisions.choice: wrote
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat "wrote" from verse 8, which the heading leaves out; Literal keeps the bare list, ending with a comma as the sentence runs on.

decisions.choice: the people of Erech, Babylon and Susa
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the cities instead of the forms "Erechites" and "Susanchites", which Literal keeps.

decisions.choice: "los dinaítas, los afarsaquitas, los tarpelitas, los afarsitas"
decisions.reason: Uncertain names or titles (m2), kept as names of peoples in Spanish form; Balanced and Readable name the cities Erec (as Genesis 10:10), Babilonia and Susa, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "watu wa Ereki, wa Babeli na wa Shushani" (B, R); Literal "Waereki ... Washushani"
decisions.reason: As the English, Balanced and Readable name the cities; "Shushani" is the usual Swahili form of Susa.

decisions.choice: người Đi-na, người A-phạt-sa-thê, người Tạt-bên, người A-phạt-sít, người Đê-ha-vê
decisions.reason: These uncertain names (m2, m4) are spelled from the Aramaic in the usual Vietnamese way. Erech keeps "Ê-rết" from Genesis 10:10 and Elam "Ê-lam" from Acts 2:9; Susa is "Su-sơ".

decisions.choice: "디나, 아바삿, 다블래, 아바새, 아렉, 수산, 데해 사람들"
decisions.reason: The names are kept as names in their usual Protestant forms; the meaning decision says that several may be titles.

decisions.choice: "편지를 썼다"
alternatives: Leaving the list without a verb
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat "wrote" from verse 8 as the English does; Literal keeps the bare list, running on into verse 10.

decisions.choice: dinaítas, afarsaquitas, tarpelitas, afarsitas, deavitas; Ereque, Susã
decisions.reason: The uncertain names (m2) are given the Portuguese ending "-itas" for peoples, written in lowercase like "elamitas". Literal says "os de Ereque", "os de Susã", since Portuguese has no ready form for the Aramaic gentilics; "Ereque" as Genesis 10:10 and "Susã", the usual Brazilian form of Susa. The forms are uncertain.

decisions.choice: Osnappar: probably Ashurbanipal, king of Assyria
decisions.reason: Osnappar is most likely Ashurbanipal, who ruled Assyria about 668 to 627 BC after Esarhaddon (verse 2). He fought against Babylon and Elam, and the peoples named in verse 9 may have been deported after those wars. The name is not found elsewhere in the Bible.

decisions.choice: Beyond the River: the Persian province west of the Euphrates
decisions.reason: "The River" is the Euphrates. Seen from the Persian capitals, the land beyond it was the province that held Syria, Phoenicia, Samaria and Judah. It is the official name of the province throughout Ezra and Nehemiah (Nehemiah 2:7).

decisions.choice: and now: and so forth
decisions.reason: The word marks a pause or move on in an Aramaic letter. Here, after the list of senders and before the narrator's "This is the copy" in verse 11, it most likely means "and so on": the narrator shortens the heading.

decisions.choice: the province Beyond the River (Balanced); the province west of the Euphrates (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Ezra term list gives these wordings; Literal keeps "Beyond the River".

decisions.choice: had taken from their homelands
decisions.reason: Readable says "deported" in plain words.

decisions.choice: "Más Allá del Río" (L); "la provincia de Más Allá del Río" (B); "la provincia al oeste del Éufrates" (R); "y ahora" (L); "etcétera" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The terms note's wording for the province; the closing word shortens the heading (m3), so Balanced and Readable say "etcétera", while Literal keeps "y ahora".

decisions.choice: "Ng'ambo ya Mto" (L), "jimbo la Ng'ambo ya Mto" (B), "jimbo lililo magharibi ya mto Frati" (R)
decisions.reason: As the terms note: "Ng'ambo ya Mto" is the name of the province (Joshua 24:3 has the phrase); Readable says where it lay.

decisions.choice: "Asnapari"
decisions.reason: The form follows the Aramaic; the meaning decision says he is most likely Ashurbanipal.

decisions.choice: "Au-delà du Fleuve" (Literal); "la province d'Au-delà du Fleuve" (Balanced); "la province à l'ouest de l'Euphrate" (Readable)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as the terms note: Literal keeps the Persian name of the province, Balanced adds that it is a province, Readable names the river.

decisions.choice: passé composé "a déportés" (Literal, Balanced)
decisions.reason: Verses 9-10 are the heading of the letter, so they take the tenses of speech, as the Aramaic letters do throughout.

decisions.choice: bên kia Sông (Literal); tỉnh Bên Kia Sông (Balanced); tỉnh phía tây sông Ơ-phơ-rát (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Beyond the River" is worded at each level as the terms note gives it and kept through Ezra: Literal as in Joshua 24:2, Balanced as the province's name, Readable saying where it lay.

decisions.choice: và bây giờ (Literal); v.v. (Balanced); Vân vân (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Aramaic word that moves a letter on (m3): Literal keeps "và bây giờ"; Balanced and Readable say "and so on".

decisions.choice: "이하 생략" (B, R) for "and now"
decisions.reason: As the meaning decision: here the word shortens the heading, "and so on"; Literal keeps the word.

decisions.choice: Além do Rio (L); a província de Além do Rio (B); a província a oeste do Eufrates (R)
decisions.reason: For Ezra-Nehemiah: the Persian province west of the Euphrates (m2) keeps its official name as a proper name at Literal and Balanced, as the English does, and Readable says where it was, as 1 Kings 5:4 in Portuguese ("a oeste do Eufrates"). decisions.choice: the copy: the text of the letter, quoted
decisions.reason: The word is a Persian term for a copy or written text of a document (verse 23; 5:6). The writer quotes the letter from records, as he quotes the other documents in these chapters.

decisions.choice: your servants: the polite self-description of officials writing to a king
decisions.reason: Those who write call themselves the king's servants, as subjects and officials of the empire did in addressing him; here it means his officials (compare 5:11).

decisions.choice: and now: the formula that turns to the business of the letter
decisions.reason: In Aramaic letters this word ends the greeting and leads into the message itself (7:12).

decisions.choice: To King Artaxerxes, from your servants
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable set out the letter's address the way an English letter would; Literal keeps the order of the Aramaic. The quotation runs to the end of verse 16.

decisions.choice: the men (Balanced); the people (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says "people", since the senders stand for the whole province; Literal and Balanced keep "men", since the writers are named officials.

decisions.choice: "A Artajerjes el rey, tus siervos ..." (L); "Al rey Artajerjes, de parte de tus siervos ..." (B, R)
decisions.reason: The address of the Aramaic letters as the terms note sets it; the king is addressed as "tú", as one person always is. The quotation runs to the end of verse 16.

decisions.reason: Literal keeps the order of the Aramaic; Balanced and Readable set the address out as a Swahili letter would. The quotation runs to the end of verse 16.

decisions.choice: "tes serviteurs": the king is addressed as "tu"
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as the terms note and Samuel: the Persian king is "tu" ("tes serviteurs") at every level, as French Bibles address kings; the letters' formulas follow the terms note.

decisions.choice: Các đầy tớ của vua (Literal); Kính tâu vua (Balanced); Kính gửi vua ... chúng tôi (Readable)
decisions.reason: The letter opens with the formulas the terms note sets for the Aramaic letters: Literal keeps the Aramaic order, Balanced the court address "Kính tâu", and Readable a plain letter heading with "chúng tôi" for the senders. "Your servants" is "các đầy tớ của vua" at every level.

decisions.choice: The officials' letter is in 합쇼체, the senders calling themselves "종들" and the king "왕" (L) or "임금님" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The terms note: officials writing to the Persian king use 합쇼체 with 임금님 and 종들, and the king's replies are in 해라체. "폐하" belongs to a later court style; "임금님" is the plain respectful word.

decisions.choice: The heading of the letter opens the quotation, which runs to the end of verse 16
alternatives: Closing the quotation in each verse
decisions.reason: As the English: the letter is one quotation over several records.

decisions.choice: os seus servos; o rei (every level)
decisions.reason: The writers address the king, and every level speaks of the king in the third person, "o rei", as Portuguese addresses a sovereign in writing and as the letter itself does ("Saiba o rei"); "Vossa Majestade" is the Portuguese courtly form, but its "vossa" belongs to the archaic "vós" that the style guide does not use, and "tu" is kept for God. The king writes to his officials with "vocês" (4:18-22), and Darius and Cyrus speak to a single subject with "você" (5:15).

source.text: יְדִ֨יעַ֙ לֶהֱוֵ֣א לְמַלְכָּ֔א דִּ֣י יְהוּדָיֵ֗א דִּ֤י סְלִ֨קוּ֙ מִן־לְוָתָ֔ךְ עֲלֶ֥ינָא אֲת֖וֹ לִירוּשְׁלֶ֑ם קִרְיְתָ֨א מָֽרָדְתָּ֤א וּבִֽישְׁתָּא֙בָּנַ֔יִן וְשׁוּרַיָּ֣א שַׁכְלִ֔ילוּ וְאֻשַּׁיָּ֖א יַחִֽיטוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Known let it be to the king that the Jews who came up from beside you to us have come to Jerusalem; the city the rebellious and the evil they are building, and the walls they have finished, and the foundations they are joining.

en.L: Let it be known to the king that the Jews who came up from you to us have come to Jerusalem. They are building the rebellious and evil city; they have finished the walls and are repairing the foundations.
en.B: Let the king know that the Jews who came up from you to us have gone to Jerusalem. They are rebuilding that rebellious and wicked city. They have finished the walls and are repairing the foundations.
en.R: We want you, the king, to know that the Jews who came here from you have arrived in Jerusalem. They are rebuilding that wicked city that is always rebelling. They have finished the walls and are repairing the foundations.

es.L: Sepa el rey que los judíos que subieron de parte tuya a nosotros han llegado a Jerusalén. Están edificando la ciudad rebelde y mala; han terminado los muros y están reparando los cimientos.
es.B: Que el rey sepa que los judíos que subieron de tu parte hacia nosotros han ido a Jerusalén. Están reconstruyendo esa ciudad rebelde y malvada. Han terminado los muros y están reparando los cimientos.
es.R: Queremos informar al rey que los judíos que vinieron de donde tú estás han llegado a Jerusalén. Están reconstruyendo esa ciudad malvada que siempre se rebela. Ya terminaron los muros y están reparando los cimientos.

fr.L: Qu’il soit connu du roi que les Juifs qui sont montés d’auprès de toi vers nous sont arrivés à Jérusalem. Ils bâtissent la ville rebelle et méchante ; ils ont achevé les murailles et ils réparent les fondations.
fr.B: Que le roi sache que les Juifs qui sont montés de chez toi vers nous sont allés à Jérusalem. Ils rebâtissent cette ville rebelle et méchante. Ils ont achevé les murailles et réparent les fondations.
fr.R: Nous voulons que tu saches, ô roi, que les Juifs qui sont venus de chez toi jusqu’ici sont arrivés à Jérusalem. Ils reconstruisent cette ville mauvaise, qui se révolte sans cesse. Ils ont fini les murailles et réparent les fondations.

sw.L: Ijulikane kwa mfalme kwamba Wayahudi waliopanda kutoka kwako kuja kwetu wamefika Yerusalemu. Wanaujenga mji ule wa uasi na mbaya; wamemaliza kuta na wanaitengeneza misingi.
sw.B: Ijulikane kwa mfalme kwamba Wayahudi waliopanda kutoka kwako kuja kwetu wamekwenda Yerusalemu. Wanaujenga upya mji ule wa uasi na mwovu. Wamemaliza kuta na wanaitengeneza misingi.
sw.R: Mfalme na ajue kwamba Wayahudi waliokuja huku kutoka kwako wamefika Yerusalemu. Wanaujenga upya mji ule mwovu ambao siku zote huasi. Wamemaliza kuta na wanaitengeneza misingi.

vi.L: Xin vua biết rằng những người Do Thái đã từ vua đi lên đến với chúng tôi, đã đến Giê-ru-sa-lem. Họ đang xây cái thành phản nghịch và độc ác ấy; họ đã làm xong các tường thành và đang sửa lại các nền móng.
vi.B: Chúng tôi xin tâu để vua biết rằng những người Do Thái từ chỗ vua lên đây với chúng tôi đã đến Giê-ru-sa-lem. Họ đang xây lại cái thành phản loạn và gian ác ấy. Họ đã làm xong tường thành và đang tu sửa nền móng.
vi.R: Chúng tôi muốn vua biết rằng những người Do Thái từ chỗ vua đến đây đã tới Giê-ru-sa-lem. Họ đang xây lại cái thành gian ác luôn luôn nổi loạn ấy. Họ đã làm xong tường thành và đang sửa lại nền móng.

ko.L: 왕께서 아시기를 바랍니다. 왕께로부터 우리에게 올라온 유대인들이 예루살렘에 이르렀습니다. 그들이 그 반역하는 악한 성읍을 건축하고 있습니다. 그들이 성벽을 완성했고 기초를 보수하고 있습니다.
ko.B: 임금님께서 아셔야 할 일이 있습니다. 임금님께로부터 저희에게로 올라온 유대인들이 예루살렘에 가서, 그 반역하는 악한 성읍을 다시 세우고 있습니다. 그들은 성벽을 다 쌓고 기초를 보수하고 있습니다.
ko.R: 임금님께 알려 드립니다. 임금님 곁을 떠나 이곳으로 온 유대인들이 예루살렘에 도착했습니다. 그들은 늘 반역을 일삼던 그 악한 성읍을 다시 세우고 있습니다. 성벽 쌓기를 마쳤고 기초를 보수하고 있습니다.

pt.L: Seja conhecido ao rei que os judeus que subiram de junto do rei a nós chegaram a Jerusalém; estão edificando a cidade rebelde e má, e terminaram os muros e estão reparando os alicerces.
pt.B: Saiba o rei que os judeus que subiram de junto do rei até nós foram para Jerusalém. Estão reconstruindo aquela cidade rebelde e perversa. Já terminaram os muros e estão reparando os alicerces.
pt.R: Queremos que o rei saiba que os judeus que vieram do lugar onde o rei está chegaram a Jerusalém. Eles estão reconstruindo aquela cidade má, que está sempre se rebelando. Já terminaram os muros e estão consertando os alicerces.

decisions.choice: the Jews who came up from you: a group that came in Artaxerxes' reign
decisions.reason: The letter speaks of Jews who had come from the king's own lands to Jerusalem in his reign. This may be the group that came with Ezra (7:1-9) or another not recorded. "Jews" here is the name used by outsiders for the people of Judah (verse 23; 5:1).

decisions.choice: they have finished the walls: the accusers overstate
decisions.reason: The verb is in a completed form: "they have finished the walls". The Hebrew margin points it slightly differently, with the same sense. Putting the finished walls before the foundations sounds like an overstatement meant to alarm the king; in verses 13 and 16 they speak of the walls being finished in the future.

decisions.choice: repairing the foundations: joining or restoring them
decisions.reason: The verb is rare; it seems to mean "to join" or "to repair", here of restoring the foundations of the wall.

decisions.choice: that rebellious and wicked city
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "that" for the Aramaic article, which here points to a city the king is supposed to know of. Readable turns "rebellious" into "always rebelling".

decisions.choice: "Sepa el rey" (L); "Que el rey sepa" (B); "Queremos informar al rey" (R)
decisions.reason: The letter formula as the terms note sets it, used through the Aramaic letters.

decisions.choice: "Ijulikane kwa mfalme" (L, B), "Mfalme na ajue" (R)
decisions.reason: The terms-note wording for the letter formula, kept wherever it returns (4:13; 5:8).

decisions.choice: Xin vua biết rằng (Literal); Chúng tôi xin tâu để vua biết (Balanced); Chúng tôi muốn vua biết (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Be it known to the king", worded as the terms note gives it for the Aramaic letters. The writers speak of the king in the third person, "vua", as subjects address a king in Kings.

source.text: כְּעַ֗ן יְדִ֨יעַ֙ לֶהֱוֵ֣א לְמַלְכָּ֔א דִּ֠י הֵ֣ן קִרְיְתָ֥א דָךְ֙ תִּתְבְּנֵ֔א וְשׁוּרַיָּ֖ה יִֽשְׁתַּכְלְל֑וּן מִנְדָּֽה־בְל֤וֹ וַהֲלָךְ֙ לָ֣א יִנְתְּנ֔וּן וְאַפְּתֹ֥ם מַלְכִ֖ים תְּהַנְזִֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: Now known let it be to the king that if the city this is built and the walls are finished, tribute, tax and toll they will not give, and at last [the revenue of the] kings it will damage.

en.L: Now let it be known to the king that if this city is built and the walls are finished, they will not pay tribute, tax or toll, and in the end it will damage the [revenue of the] kings.
en.B: Now let the king know that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are finished, they will not pay tribute, tax or duty, and in the end the royal revenue will suffer.
en.R: You should also know that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are finished, the people will stop paying taxes of every kind, and in the end the king will lose money.

es.L: Ahora sepa el rey que si esta ciudad es edificada y los muros terminados, no pagarán tributo, impuesto ni peaje, y al final perjudicará [las rentas de] los reyes.
es.B: Ahora, que el rey sepa que si esta ciudad es reconstruida y sus muros terminados, no pagarán tributo, impuesto ni peaje, y al final el tesoro real saldrá perjudicado.
es.R: También debes saber que, si esta ciudad es reconstruida y sus muros terminados, la gente dejará de pagar toda clase de impuestos, y al final el rey perderá dinero.

fr.L: Maintenant, qu’il soit connu du roi que, si cette ville est bâtie et que les murailles sont achevées, ils ne paieront ni tribut, ni impôt, ni droit de passage, et à la fin cela causera du tort aux [revenus des] rois.
fr.B: Que le roi sache donc que, si cette ville est rebâtie et ses murailles achevées, ils ne paieront plus ni tribut, ni impôt, ni taxe, et à la fin les revenus royaux en souffriront.
fr.R: Sache aussi que, si cette ville est reconstruite et que ses murailles sont terminées, les gens arrêteront de payer toutes sortes d’impôts, et à la fin le roi perdra de l’argent.

sw.L: Basi ijulikane kwa mfalme kwamba mji huu ukijengwa na kuta zikimalizika, hawatalipa kodi, ushuru wala ada, na mwishowe utaidhuru [hazina ya] wafalme.
sw.B: Basi ijulikane kwa mfalme kwamba mji huu ukijengwa upya na kuta zake zikimalizika, hawatalipa kodi, ushuru wala ada, na mwishowe mapato ya mfalme yatapungua.
sw.R: Pia unapaswa kujua kwamba mji huu ukijengwa upya na kuta zake zikimalizika, watu wataacha kulipa kodi za kila aina, na mwishowe mfalme atapoteza fedha.

vi.L: Bây giờ xin vua biết rằng nếu thành này được xây và các tường thành được hoàn tất, thì họ sẽ không nộp cống phẩm, thuế hay lệ phí, và cuối cùng điều ấy sẽ gây thiệt hại cho [ngân khố của] các vua.
vi.B: Nay xin vua biết rằng nếu thành này được xây lại và tường thành được hoàn tất, thì họ sẽ không nộp cống phẩm, thuế hay lệ phí, và cuối cùng ngân khố của vua sẽ bị thiệt hại.
vi.R: Vua cũng nên biết rằng nếu thành này được xây lại và tường thành được làm xong, dân ấy sẽ không nộp bất cứ thứ thuế nào nữa, và cuối cùng vua sẽ mất tiền.

ko.L: 이제 왕께서 아시기를 바랍니다. 만일 이 성읍이 건축되고 성벽이 완성되면, 그들이 조공과 세금과 통행세를 바치지 않을 것이고, 결국 왕들[의 수입]에 손해를 끼칠 것입니다.
ko.B: 이제 임금님께서 아셔야 합니다. 이 성읍이 다시 세워지고 성벽이 완성되면, 그들은 조공도 세금도 관세도 바치지 않을 것이고, 결국 왕실 수입이 줄어들 것입니다.
ko.R: 또 이것도 아셔야 합니다. 이 성읍이 다시 세워지고 성벽이 완성되면, 그 백성은 어떤 세금도 내지 않을 것입니다. 그러면 결국 임금님께서 손해를 보시게 됩니다.

pt.L: Agora seja conhecido ao rei que, se esta cidade for edificada e os muros forem terminados, não pagarão tributo, imposto nem pedágio, e no fim isso prejudicará os [rendimentos dos] reis.
pt.B: Saiba agora o rei que, se esta cidade for reconstruída e os seus muros forem terminados, eles não pagarão tributo, imposto nem pedágio, e no fim a renda real sofrerá prejuízo.
pt.R: O rei também deve saber que, se esta cidade for reconstruída e os seus muros forem terminados, o povo vai deixar de pagar impostos de todo tipo, e no fim o rei vai perder dinheiro.

decisions.choice: tribute, tax and toll: the kinds of royal tax
decisions.reason: The three words cover the taxes of the Persian empire: a payment in money, a tax on goods or produce, and a toll or land tax. Exactly which was which is not certain; together they mean every kind of tax due to the king (verse 20; 7:24).

decisions.choice: at last it will damage kings: the royal treasury will lose
alternatives: surely it will damage the kings
decisions.reason: The word for "at last" is a Persian loanword that may mean "in the end" or "surely". "Kings" here stands for the royal house and its income; the sentence is short, and the sense must be filled out.

decisions.choice: taxes of every kind
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the three tax words together (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "조공과 세금과 통행세" (L), "조공도 세금도 관세도" (B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the three kinds of royal tax, as the English does; Readable says "어떤 세금도", taxes of every kind (meaning decision m1).

source.text: כְּעַ֗ן כָּל־קֳבֵל֙ דִּֽי־מְלַ֤ח הֵֽיכְלָא֙ מְלַ֔חְנָא וְעַרְוַ֣ת מַלְכָּ֔א לָ֥א אֲֽרִֽיךְ לַ֖נָא לְמֶֽחֱזֵ֑א עַ֨ל־דְּנָ֔ה שְׁלַ֖חְנָא וְהוֹדַ֥עְנָא לְמַלְכָּֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: Now, because that [the] salt of the palace we eat, and [the] nakedness of the king not [is] fitting for us to see, for this we have sent and made known to the king,

en.L: Now, because we eat the salt of the palace, and it is not fitting for us to see the dishonor of the king, therefore we have sent and made known to the king,
en.B: Now because we are bound to the palace by salt, and it is not right for us to watch the king being dishonored, we have sent to inform the king,
en.R: Since we are loyal to the king and are paid by the palace, it is not right for us to see the king dishonored. That is why we are sending this message to inform you,

es.L: Ahora bien, puesto que comemos la sal del palacio, y no nos es propio ver la deshonra del rey, por esto hemos enviado a informar al rey,
es.B: Ahora bien, como estamos unidos al palacio por la sal, y no está bien que veamos deshonrar al rey, hemos enviado a informar al rey,
es.R: Como somos leales al rey y el palacio nos paga, no está bien que veamos que el rey es deshonrado. Por eso enviamos este mensaje para informarte,

fr.L: Maintenant, parce que nous mangeons le sel du palais et qu’il ne nous convient pas de voir le déshonneur du roi, à cause de cela nous avons envoyé informer le roi,
fr.B: Or, puisque nous sommes liés au palais par le sel et qu’il ne nous convient pas de voir le roi déshonoré, nous envoyons informer le roi,
fr.R: Puisque nous sommes fidèles au roi et payés par le palais, il n’est pas juste que nous voyions le roi déshonoré. C’est pourquoi nous t’envoyons ce message pour t’informer,

sw.L: Basi, kwa kuwa tunakula chumvi ya ikulu, na haitufai kuona aibu ya mfalme, kwa hiyo tumetuma na kumjulisha mfalme,
sw.B: Basi kwa kuwa tumefungwa na ikulu kwa chumvi, na si haki kwetu kumwona mfalme akiaibishwa, tumetuma kumjulisha mfalme,
sw.R: Kwa kuwa sisi ni waaminifu kwa mfalme na tunalipwa na ikulu, si haki kwetu kumwona mfalme akiaibishwa. Ndiyo sababu tunatuma ujumbe huu kukujulisha,

vi.L: Bây giờ, vì chúng tôi ăn muối của cung điện, và không phải lẽ cho chúng tôi nhìn thấy sự sỉ nhục của vua, vì vậy chúng tôi đã sai người tâu cho vua biết,
vi.B: Nay vì chúng tôi đã ăn muối của triều đình, và không thể đứng nhìn vua bị sỉ nhục, nên chúng tôi sai người tâu lên vua,
vi.R: Vì chúng tôi trung thành với vua và được triều đình cấp dưỡng, chúng tôi không thể đứng nhìn vua bị sỉ nhục. Vì thế, chúng tôi gửi thư này để tâu cho vua biết,

ko.L: 이제 우리가 궁전의 소금을 먹고 있으므로, 왕께서 수치를 당하시는 것을 보는 것이 우리에게 마땅하지 않습니다. 그러므로 우리가 사람을 보내어 왕께 알려 드립니다.
ko.B: 저희는 왕궁의 소금을 먹는 사람들이므로, 임금님께서 욕을 당하시는 것을 보고만 있을 수 없습니다. 그래서 이렇게 사람을 보내어 임금님께 알려 드립니다.
ko.R: 저희는 왕궁에서 녹을 받으며 임금님께 충성하는 사람들입니다. 그러니 임금님께서 욕을 당하시는 것을 그냥 보고 있을 수 없습니다. 그래서 이 편지를 보내 알려 드립니다.

pt.L: Agora, porque comemos o sal do palácio, e não nos convém ver a desonra do rei, por isso enviamos e fizemos [isto] conhecido ao rei,
pt.B: Ora, como estamos ligados ao palácio pelo sal, e não é certo que vejamos o rei ser desonrado, mandamos informar o rei,
pt.R: Nós somos leais ao rei e recebemos o nosso sustento do palácio. Por isso não é certo vermos o rei ser desonrado. É por isso que estamos mandando esta mensagem para informar o rei,

decisions.choice: we eat the salt of the palace: we are in the king's service and bound to him
decisions.reason: To eat someone's salt was to receive his provision and owe him loyalty; salt was a sign of a binding agreement (Numbers 18:19; 2 Chronicles 13:5). The writers present themselves as loyal servants of the crown.

decisions.choice: the nakedness of the king: the king's dishonor
decisions.reason: "Nakedness" here is shame or disgrace: a loss of the king's honor and power.

decisions.choice: ending with a comma
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into verse 15 ("so that a search may be made"), so Literal and Balanced end the record with a comma.

decisions.choice: bound to the palace by salt (Balanced); loyal to the king and paid by the palace (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "eat the salt of the palace"; Balanced keeps the picture and says what it implies, Readable gives the sense only.

decisions.choice: "comemos la sal del palacio" (L); "estamos unidos al palacio por la sal" (B); "somos leales al rey y el palacio nos paga" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture, Balanced keeps it and says what it implies, Readable gives the sense only (m1), as the English does.

decisions.choice: "tumefungwa na ikulu kwa chumvi" (B); "sisi ni waaminifu kwa mfalme na tunalipwa na ikulu" (R); Literal "tunakula chumvi ya ikulu"
decisions.reason: As the English: Balanced keeps the picture and says what it implies; Readable gives the sense only.

decisions.choice: ăn muối của cung điện (Literal); ăn muối của triều đình (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the picture of eating the palace's salt, which says that they are bound to the king (m1); Readable says it plainly.

records.literal_gloss: that one may search in [the] book of the records of your fathers, and you will find in [the] book of the records and know that the city this [is] a city rebellious and damaging kings and provinces, and revolt they have been making in its midst from [the] days of old; on this [account] the city this was laid waste.

en.L: so that search may be made in the book of the records of your fathers. And you will find in the book of the records and know that this city is a rebellious city, harmful to kings and provinces, and they have made revolt within it from days of old; for this reason this city was laid waste.
en.B: so that a search may be made in the record books of your predecessors. You will find in the records and learn that this city is a rebellious city, harmful to kings and provinces, a place of revolt from ancient times. That is why this city was destroyed.
en.R: so that you can have the records of the kings before you searched. In them you will find that this city has always rebelled. It has caused trouble for kings and provinces, and its people have rebelled against their rulers since long ago. That is why this city was destroyed.

es.L: para que se busque en el libro de las memorias de tus padres. Y hallarás en el libro de las memorias y sabrás que esta ciudad es una ciudad rebelde y dañina para los reyes y las provincias, y que dentro de ella se han hecho rebeliones desde tiempos antiguos; por esto esta ciudad fue destruida.
es.B: para que se busque en los libros de las memorias de tus predecesores. En las memorias encontrarás y sabrás que esta ciudad es una ciudad rebelde, dañina para los reyes y las provincias, un lugar de rebeliones desde tiempos antiguos. Por eso esta ciudad fue destruida.
es.R: para que mandes buscar en los registros de los reyes que estuvieron antes que tú. En ellos encontrarás que esta ciudad siempre se ha rebelado. Ha causado problemas a reyes y provincias, y su gente se ha rebelado contra sus gobernantes desde hace mucho tiempo. Por eso esta ciudad fue destruida.

fr.L: afin qu’on fasse des recherches dans le livre des annales de tes pères. Et tu trouveras dans le livre des annales et tu sauras que cette ville est une ville rebelle, nuisible aux rois et aux provinces, et qu’on y a fait des révoltes depuis les jours anciens ; c’est pour cela que cette ville a été dévastée.
fr.B: afin qu’on fasse des recherches dans les livres des annales de tes prédécesseurs. Tu trouveras dans les annales et tu apprendras que cette ville est une ville rebelle, nuisible aux rois et aux provinces, un lieu de révolte depuis les temps anciens. C’est pour cela que cette ville a été détruite.
fr.R: afin que tu fasses chercher dans les archives des rois qui t’ont précédé. Tu y trouveras que cette ville s’est toujours révoltée. Elle a causé des problèmes aux rois et aux provinces, et ses habitants se révoltent contre leurs dirigeants depuis très longtemps. C’est pour cela que cette ville a été détruite.

sw.L: ili utafutaji ufanyike katika kitabu cha kumbukumbu za baba zako. Nawe utaona katika kitabu cha kumbukumbu na kujua kwamba mji huu ni mji wa uasi, wenye kuwadhuru wafalme na majimbo, nao wamefanya maasi ndani yake tangu siku za kale; kwa sababu hiyo mji huu uliharibiwa.
sw.B: ili utafutaji ufanyike katika vitabu vya kumbukumbu vya watangulizi wako. Utaona katika kumbukumbu hizo na kujua kwamba mji huu ni mji wa uasi, wenye kuwadhuru wafalme na majimbo, mahali pa maasi tangu zamani za kale. Ndiyo sababu mji huu uliharibiwa.

vi.L: để người ta tìm trong sách ghi chép của các tổ phụ vua. Và vua sẽ tìm thấy trong sách ghi chép và biết rằng thành này là một thành phản nghịch, gây hại cho các vua và các tỉnh, và người ta đã gây loạn trong đó từ những ngày xa xưa; vì lý do ấy mà thành này đã bị phá hủy.
vi.B: để vua cho tra cứu sách biên niên của các tiên vương. Vua sẽ thấy trong sách biên niên và biết rằng thành này là một thành phản loạn, gây hại cho các vua và các tỉnh, là nơi nổi loạn từ thời xa xưa. Chính vì thế mà thành này đã bị phá hủy.
vi.R: để vua cho tra cứu sách ghi chép của các vua trước. Trong đó, vua sẽ thấy rằng thành này luôn luôn nổi loạn. Thành ấy đã gây rắc rối cho các vua và các tỉnh, và dân thành ấy đã chống lại các vua cai trị họ từ xưa. Vì thế mà thành này đã bị phá hủy.

ko.L: 그러니 왕의 조상들의 기록책을 조사하게 하십시오. 그러면 그 기록책에서 이 성읍이 반역하는 성읍이요, 왕들과 지방들에 해를 끼치는 성읍이며, 옛날부터 그 안에서 반란을 일으켜 왔다는 것을 찾아 알게 되실 것입니다. 이 때문에 이 성읍이 황폐하게 되었습니다.
ko.B: 그러니 임금님의 선왕들의 기록 문서를 찾아보게 하십시오. 그러면 그 기록에서 이 성읍이 반역하는 성읍이요 왕들과 지방들에 해를 끼쳐 온 성읍이며, 옛날부터 반란이 끊이지 않던 곳임을 아시게 될 것입니다. 바로 그 때문에 이 성읍이 멸망했던 것입니다.
ko.R: 그러니 이전 왕들의 기록을 찾아보게 하십시오. 그 기록을 보시면, 이 성읍이 늘 반역해 왔다는 것을 아시게 될 것입니다. 이 성읍은 왕들과 여러 지방에 골칫거리였고, 그곳 백성은 오래전부터 통치자들에게 반란을 일으켰습니다. 그래서 이 성읍이 멸망했던 것입니다.

pt.L: para que se procure no livro dos registros dos pais do rei. E [o rei] achará no livro dos registros e saberá que esta cidade [é] uma cidade rebelde, prejudicial aos reis e às províncias, e fizeram revolta dentro dela desde os dias antigos; por isso esta cidade foi destruída.
pt.B: para que se faça uma busca nos livros de registros dos antecessores do rei. Nos registros o rei achará e saberá que esta cidade é uma cidade rebelde, prejudicial aos reis e às províncias, um lugar de revoltas desde tempos antigos. Foi por isso que esta cidade foi destruída.
pt.R: para que o rei mande procurar nos registros dos reis que vieram antes dele. Neles o rei vai descobrir que esta cidade sempre se rebelou. Ela tem causado problemas para reis e províncias, e o seu povo se revolta contra os seus governantes desde muito tempo atrás. É por isso que esta cidade foi destruída.

decisions.choice: your fathers: the kings before you
decisions.reason: "Fathers" means predecessors on the throne, not only the king's own ancestors. The Persian kings kept the records of the Babylonian kings before them (compare 5:17; 6:1-2).

decisions.choice: a rebellious city, laid waste: Jerusalem's history against Assyria and Babylon
decisions.reason: Kings of Judah rebelled against Assyria (2 Kings 18:7) and against Babylon (2 Kings 24:1, 20), and Babylon destroyed the city in 586 BC (2 Kings 25:8-10). The letter is hostile, but its history is true.

decisions.choice: your predecessors (Balanced); the kings before you (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "your fathers" (meaning decision m1); Literal keeps "fathers".

decisions.choice: "tus predecesores" (B); "los reyes que estuvieron antes que tú" (R); "tus padres" (L)
decisions.reason: The sense of "your fathers" (m1), as the English gives it; Literal keeps "padres".

decisions.choice: sách ghi chép (Literal, Readable); sách biên niên (Balanced)
decisions.reason: The royal records are "sách ghi chép" or "sách biên niên", never "Sử Ký", which is only the title of Chronicles.

decisions.choice: các tiên vương
decisions.reason: "Your fathers" means the kings before him (m1); Balanced says "các tiên vương", the former kings, and Readable "các vua trước".

decisions.choice: "기록책" (L), "기록 문서" (B), "이전 왕들의 기록" (R) for "the book of the records"
decisions.reason: The terms note's forms; "역대기" is kept for the title of Chronicles. "선왕들" (B) and "이전 왕들" (R) give the sense of "your fathers", as the English does.

records.literal_gloss: Making known [are] we to the king that if the city this is built and the walls are finished, on account of this a portion in Beyond the River there will not be to you.

en.L: We are making known to the king that if this city is built and the walls are finished, because of this you will have no portion in Beyond the River."
en.B: We are informing the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are finished, you will no longer have any possession in the province Beyond the River."
en.R: We want you to know that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are finished, you will lose control of the whole province west of the Euphrates."

decisions.choice: no portion in Beyond the River: the king will lose the province
decisions.reason: "Portion" is a share or possession. The writers claim that one rebuilt city would cost the king his hold on the whole province, a great overstatement meant to alarm him.

decisions.choice: lose control of the whole province
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the idiom (meaning decision m1).
